study_identification_part.si_4_title: Patterns of connectome variability in autism across five functional activation tasks: findings from the LEAP project

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used the EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS LEAP (Longitudinal European Autism Project) dataset, which is a large multi-center European project. Data were acquired at 6 sites: King's College London (KCL), Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre (RUNMC), University Medical Centre Utrecht (UMCU), Autism Research Centre/University of Cambridge (ARC/UCAM), Central Institute of Mental Health Mannheim (CIMH), and Karolinska Institutet (KI). Data from KI were not used due to low number of participants. This is a MULTI-SITE study with specific dataset name LEAP.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The dataset from the EU-AIMS/AIMS2TRIALS LEAP project was used for the current analyses-a large multicenter European project with an aim to identify biomarkers in [18-20]." ... "MRI data were acquired on 3T scanners at multiple sites in Europe-King's College London (KCL), Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre (RUNMC), University Medical Centre Utrecht (UMCU), Autism Research Centre (ARC), University of Cambridge (UCAM), Central Institute of Mental Health, Mannheim (CIMH), and Karolinska Institutet (KI). Data from KI were not used due to a low number of participants."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Looden2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Sample, L53-56 and L63-64

answer.LEAP: normative model training/testing (TD participants) and clinical autism application (ASD participants)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The LEAP dataset served dual purposes: (1) Typically developing (TD) controls (n=221) were used to build the normative model of task potency edge values against age and sex; (2) Both TD and autism (ASD, n=282) participants were evaluated as out-of-sample for atypicality assessment. The normative model was used to predict the range of (a)typical edge values in out-of-sample TD participants and ASD participants. CCA analysis was performed only in individuals with autism to assess brain-behavior relationships.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "A normative model of potency edge values was built against age and sex from typically developing participants using the nispat implementation in python [14, 46]." ... "The model was used to predict the range of (a)typical edge values in out-of-sample typically developing participants as well as the autistic participants." ... "CCA analysis was done only in the individuals with autism in order to assess whether the variation in the task atypicality patterns relates also to phenotypic description in individuals with autism."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Looden2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Normative modelling, L75-77; Canonical correlation analysis, L83-85

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study used 221 typically developing (TD) controls for building the normative model. The paper does not explicitly separate train/validation/test splits for the normative model construction. The text states the model was built from TD participants and used to predict out-of-sample values, but specific train phase numbers are not reported. The same normative modeling approach was applied across all five fMRI tasks (Hariri, Flanker, Reward_s, Reward_ns, ToM) but constitutes a single model approach applied separately to each task.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The above criteria resulted in the inclusion of data for analyses from the following participants: 282 participants with autism (age range 7.5-30.3 years; mean=17.1; sd=5.4; 72.3% male), and 221 typically developing controls (age range 6.9-29.8 years; mean=17.0; sd=5.5; 63.8% male)." ... "A normative model of potency edge values was built against age and sex from typically developing participants using the nispat implementation in python [14, 46]."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are provided for the overall TD sample used in normative modeling. Mean age was 17.0 years with SD of 5.5 years, and range from 6.9 to 29.8 years. The paper does not report separate train-phase age statistics as no explicit train/test split is described for the normative model building process. Note that not all participants completed all fMRI tasks, so subsample sizes varied by task (see supplementary tables), but TD age statistics per task are not explicitly provided.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "221 typically developing controls (age range 6.9-29.8 years; mean=17.0; sd=5.5; 63.8% male). Not every participant was included in each analysis, for the reason that not all participants completed all fMRI scan sessions."

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper reports 63.8% male for the TD sample of 221 participants. From this, male_n is calculated as 221 * 0.638 = 141 (rounded), and female_n is 221 - 141 = 80. Female percentage is 100% - 63.8% = 36.2%. Train-phase specific sex breakdown is not reported as no explicit train/test split is described.
